newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says '96 GNP growth seen exceeding 7.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila says '96 GNP growth seen exceeding 7.1 pct.

text.p: The Philippines was expected to post a gross national product (GNP) growth rate of over 7.1 percent in 1996, up from 5.3 percent last year, Socio Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said on Friday.
"It's very likely that we will extend the surge in the fourth quarter this year," Habito told reporters at a year-end briefing.
Earlier, at the start of the briefing,, Habito had said GNP growth in 1997 was expected between 7.0 to 8.0 percent.

For 1996, the government had earlier set a GNP growth target of 6.5 percent to 7.5 percent. Last month, the government said GNP growth in the first nine months of the year was an annualised 7.1 percent.
"Early indications from exports and value of production indices have shown much stronger figures (in the fourth quarter) than in the past three quarters," Habito said.
